doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Billy Taylor for Prestige and recording in the Hackensack living room
summary: He recorded Billy Taylor for Prestige in the living room, with an upright and later a grand piano bought used.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And just before that relationship, Billy Taylor came to you and you recorded for Prestige.
Yes, Billy Taylor for Prestige. I’m not sure Billy came through me, I’m not sure, and he might have come through Bob Weinstock, the owner of Prestige Records.
Anyway, I recorded Billy Taylor a number of times, many hours spent in that living room, hearing Billy play.
Well Billy said what he really appreciated was the fact that you really wanted to experiment with the sound and get the real sound.
We had the same ideas, which was what we wanted the finished product to be.
Was that when you had the upright?
No, no there was a grand piano by that time, the one that I purchased from the New York Times ad.
Okay, so before the grand piano you had an upright. And that’s when you started to do the first of the Blue Note recordings?

No. That’s when I first did my friends recording. All of that time was just non­ professional fun type things for friends. We all liked the music; we knew what we wanted it to sound like, part of that was on an upright. And then I found this piano, which was a really good one, I bought that one used, it was rarely used. I got it out of a bad divorce and I got the piano. It was someone else’s divorce, not mine.
